roles.title: API Test Engineer
roles.overview: An API Test Engineer verifies application programming interfaces directly, below the user interface, where most business logic lives. The role combines manual exploration of APIs with tools like Postman and, increasingly, automated suites. It is a natural step for manual testers who want more technical depth without starting with complex UI automation.
responsibilities: Read API specifications such as OpenAPI documents and derive test cases
Test endpoints for functional behaviour, validation, errors and authorisation
Build and maintain Postman collections with environments and assertions
Verify API side effects in the database
Run collections in CI with Newman or automated code-based tests
Report API defects with full request and response evidence

essential: HTTP methods, status codes and headers
roleSpecific: Negative and boundary testing of APIs
optional: Code-based API automation with REST Assured or pytest

prerequisites: Basic understanding of how web applications communicate

beginner.title: HTTP and Postman
goals: Explain each HTTP method and when it is used
Interpret common status codes correctly
Send requests and write basic tests in Postman

intermediate.title: Thorough API testing
goals: Chain requests using variables and scripts
Test authentication and authorisation for each endpoint
Design negative and boundary cases for payloads
Verify persisted data with SQL

advanced.title: Automate and integrate
goals: Run collections in CI with Newman
Validate responses against JSON Schema
Begin a code-based API suite

tools: Swagger UI or another OpenAPI viewer
exercises: Build a Postman collection for a public practice API with tests on status, body and response time
Write ten negative payload tests for a create-user endpoint
Test that a regular user cannot access or modify another user's resources

sampleProject.title: Postman suite for a bookstore API
sampleProject.description: Run an open-source REST API locally and build a Postman collection covering CRUD, validation errors, authentication and authorisation, with environments for local and CI. Add schema checks, SQL verification notes, a Newman run in GitHub Actions, and defect reports for any issues found.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test a GET /users/{id} endpoint?
interviewQuestions.a: I would check a valid ID returns 200 with the correct user and schema, a non-existent ID returns 404, and malformed IDs return 400 or 404 as documented. I would test that unauthenticated calls return 401 and that a user cannot fetch another user's data unless permitted. I would also confirm sensitive fields like password hashes are never returned.

interviewQuestions.q: What does idempotent mean, and which methods are idempotent?
interviewQuestions.a: An idempotent operation has the same effect on server state whether it is performed once or several times. GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS are defined as idempotent; POST is not, and PATCH is not guaranteed to be. Testing this matters for retries after network failures.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you chain requests in Postman?
interviewQuestions.a: In a test or post-response script I extract a value from the response, such as an ID or token, and store it with pm.collectionVariables.set or pm.environment.set. Later requests reference it with double curly braces. This lets a collection create, read, update and delete the same resource in sequence.

interviewQuestions.q: Why test APIs instead of only testing through the UI?
interviewQuestions.a: APIs expose business logic directly, so tests are faster, more stable and pinpoint failures more precisely. They also reach cases the UI prevents, such as invalid payloads that a malicious client could send. The UI still needs some testing, but API tests catch many defects earlier and cheaper.

interviewQuestions.q: What would you include in an API defect report?
interviewQuestions.a: The method, full URL, relevant headers with secrets redacted, request body, actual status and response body, expected result with reference to the specification, environment and timestamp or correlation ID. A curl command or exported Postman request lets developers reproduce it immediately.

roles.codingRequirements: Light: Postman scripting in JavaScript and basic SQL. Code-based automation is a plus, not a requirement.
commonMistakes: Only testing happy paths with valid tokens
Not knowing which methods are idempotent
Including real secrets in shared collections or reports
readinessCriteria: You can design positive, negative and authorisation tests for any endpoint from its specification
You have a Postman collection with chained requests running via Newman in CI
You can verify an API's database side effects with SQL

roles.title: REST API Tester
roles.overview: A REST API Tester specialises in the conventions and pitfalls of RESTful HTTP APIs: resource modelling, method semantics, status codes, caching, pagination and error formats. Beyond checking that endpoints work, they check that APIs behave consistently and according to HTTP standards, which matters greatly for API consumers. It is common in teams that publish APIs to partners or the public.
responsibilities: Verify endpoints follow REST and HTTP semantics consistently
Test pagination, sorting, filtering and query parameters
Validate error response formats and messages
Check caching, content negotiation and relevant headers
Test versioning and backwards compatibility of API changes
Review API documentation against actual behaviour

essential: Detailed HTTP semantics (methods, status codes, headers)
Postman or an equivalent API client
roleSpecific: Pagination, filtering and sorting edge cases

prerequisites: Understanding of HTTP requests and responses

beginner.title: REST fundamentals
goals: Explain resources, representations and statelessness
Map CRUD operations to HTTP methods and status codes
Test a simple REST API with Postman

intermediate.title: REST details
goals: Test pagination boundaries and stable ordering
Test filter and sort parameter combinations
Validate consistent error formats across endpoints

advanced.title: Consumer-grade APIs
goals: Test idempotency keys and retry behaviour
Verify rate limiting responses and headers
Assess backwards compatibility of an API change

exercises: Test a paginated endpoint for first, last, empty and out-of-range pages, and for duplicates across pages
Compare error responses across five endpoints and report inconsistencies
Verify an endpoint's documented behaviour against actual responses and list mismatches

sampleProject.title: REST conformance review of an API
sampleProject.description: Choose an open-source REST API you can run locally. Produce a conformance test suite covering method semantics, status codes, pagination, filtering, error formats and caching headers, plus a short review report listing deviations from REST conventions and documentation mismatches with evidence.

interviewQuestions.q: What status code should a successful POST that creates a resource return?
interviewQuestions.a: Typically 201 Created, with the new resource or its identifier in the body and often a Location header pointing to it. Some APIs return 200 or 202 for valid reasons, such as asynchronous creation with 202 Accepted. I test against the documented contract and flag inconsistency across endpoints.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test pagination?
interviewQuestions.a: I check page size defaults and limits, the first and last pages, empty results, invalid values such as negative or very large page numbers, and that total counts are correct. I also verify ordering is stable, so items are not duplicated or skipped across pages, including when data changes between requests.

interviewQuestions.q: What does 'stateless' mean in REST?
interviewQuestions.a: Each request contains all the information the server needs to process it; the server does not rely on stored client session context between requests. Authentication is therefore sent with each request, for example as a token. It simplifies scaling and makes each request independently testable.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test rate limiting?
interviewQuestions.a: Send requests above the documented limit within the window in a controlled test environment and verify the API returns 429 Too Many Requests, ideally with a Retry-After header or rate limit headers if documented. Then confirm requests succeed again after the window. I also check limits apply per the intended key, such as per user or per token.

interviewQuestions.q: What makes an API change backwards incompatible?
interviewQuestions.a: Removing or renaming fields, changing types or formats, making optional fields required, changing status codes or error formats, or changing default behaviour. Adding optional fields is usually compatible, provided clients ignore unknown fields. Contract tests and versioning policies help catch breaking changes.

roles.codingRequirements: Light: Postman scripting; code-based automation helpful but not required.
commonMistakes: Treating any 2xx response as correct
Ignoring ordering stability when testing pagination
Not checking error response bodies
readinessCriteria: You can explain correct status codes for common CRUD scenarios with exceptions
You have tested pagination, filtering and rate limiting on a real API
You can identify breaking versus non-breaking API changes

roles.title: Backend Test Engineer
roles.overview: A Backend Test Engineer tests server-side systems as a whole: services, APIs, databases, caches, queues and scheduled jobs. The role needs enough programming to write automated tests and harnesses, and enough systems knowledge to reason about concurrency, transactions and failure. It is typically code-heavy and close to backend development teams.
responsibilities: Design and automate tests for backend services and their data stores
Test business logic, data integrity and transactional behaviour
Test background jobs, scheduled tasks and asynchronous processing
Use containers to run dependencies for integration tests
Investigate defects using logs, metrics and database state
Collaborate with developers on unit and integration test coverage

essential: Programming in a backend language such as Java or Python
SQL and database concepts including transactions

beginner.title: Backend foundations
goals: Automate API tests in code
Write SQL with joins and aggregates to verify results
Run a service and its database in Docker

intermediate.title: Integrity and isolation
goals: Test transactional behaviour and rollback on failure
Simulate external dependencies with stubs
Test concurrent updates to the same record

advanced.title: Distributed backends
goals: Test services that communicate asynchronously
Identify database and caching bottlenecks
Run backend suites in CI with containerised dependencies

tools: A log tool such as Kibana or Grafana Loki
exercises: Write an integration test that starts a database with Testcontainers and verifies a service's repository layer
Send two concurrent updates to the same resource and check for lost updates
Force a dependency failure mid-transaction and verify nothing partial is committed

sampleProject.title: Backend integration suite with Testcontainers
sampleProject.description: For an open-source backend service, build automated tests that start real dependencies with Testcontainers, cover API behaviour, transactional integrity, a concurrency scenario and an external dependency stubbed with WireMock, and run in CI. Document the test design and any defects found.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you test that a money transfer is atomic?
interviewQuestions.a: I would cause a failure partway through, such as the credit step failing after the debit, using a stub or fault injection in a test environment. Then I verify neither account changed and no partial records exist. I would also test concurrent transfers on the same account to check balances stay consistent.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test a scheduled job?
interviewQuestions.a: I prefer to trigger the job directly or control the clock in a test environment rather than waiting for the schedule. I prepare data covering normal, boundary and invalid cases, run the job, and verify outputs, side effects and logs. I also test re-running the job to ensure it is safe and does not duplicate work.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a lost update and how would you test for it?
interviewQuestions.a: A lost update occurs when two concurrent transactions read the same value and both write, so one change overwrites the other. I test by sending concurrent updates to the same record and checking the final state reflects both or that one is rejected, for example via optimistic locking returning a conflict.

interviewQuestions.q: Why use Testcontainers rather than an in-memory database?
interviewQuestions.a: Testcontainers runs the real database engine, so SQL dialect, constraints and transaction behaviour match production. In-memory substitutes can behave differently and hide defects. The trade-off is slower start-up, which can be reduced by reusing containers across tests.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you debug a failing backend test?
interviewQuestions.a: Reproduce it in isolation, then inspect the request, response, application logs around the correlation ID, and database state at the point of failure. I check whether test data or timing is responsible before concluding it is a product defect.

roles.codingRequirements: Moderate to strong: backend language proficiency (Java, Python, C# or Go), SQL including transactions, and comfort with Docker.
commonMistakes: Testing only through APIs without checking data integrity
Using fixed sleeps for asynchronous processing
Ignoring concurrency entirely
readinessCriteria: You have written integration tests with real dependencies in containers
You can design and run a concurrency test and explain the result
You can verify transactional integrity after an injected failure

roles.title: Integration Test Engineer
roles.overview: An Integration Test Engineer builds automated tests for the interactions between services, databases, message brokers and third-party systems. Compared with a manual integration tester, this role engineers the harnesses, stubs and environments that make integration tests reliable and repeatable. It is central in systems with many moving parts.
responsibilities: Automate tests that cover service-to-service and service-to-dependency interactions
Build stubs and simulators for third-party systems
Manage integration environments and test data across systems
Test failure handling such as timeouts, retries and partial failures
Integrate tests into CI with containerised dependencies
Work with teams on interface agreements and contract tests

essential: Test doubles: stubs, mocks and fakes
roleSpecific: Fault injection for timeouts and errors

beginner.title: Integration basics
goals: Explain integration test approaches and scopes
Automate API calls across two services
Run multiple services with Docker Compose

intermediate.title: Control dependencies
goals: Stub a third-party API with configurable responses
Test retries and timeouts deterministically
Manage test data across services

advanced.title: Reliable integration at scale
goals: Replace brittle end-to-end tests with contract tests where appropriate
Run integration suites in CI
Trace failures across services

tools: OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing tools such as Jaeger
exercises: Stub a payment provider and test success, decline, timeout and malformed responses
Test a retry policy by making a stub fail twice then succeed, and verify exactly one side effect
Use correlation IDs to trace a failing request across two services

sampleProject.title: Integration harness for a two-service system
sampleProject.description: Build a Docker Compose environment with two services, a database and a WireMock stub for an external API. Write automated integration tests for success paths, timeouts, retries and partial failures, verify data consistency, and run the suite in CI with logs collected as artefacts.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test retry logic without flaky tests?
interviewQuestions.a: Use a stub that can be scripted to fail a set number of times and then succeed, so the scenario is deterministic. Verify the number of attempts, the backoff behaviour if observable, and that the side effect happens exactly once. Avoid relying on real network failures.

interviewQuestions.q: What are the trade-offs of end-to-end integration environments?
interviewQuestions.a: They give realistic confidence but are expensive, shared, slow to set up and often unstable because many services and data sets change at once. Containerised, per-run environments and contract tests reduce the reliance on shared environments. A small set of tests in a full environment remains useful.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the difference between a fake and a stub?
interviewQuestions.a: A stub returns predefined responses to specific calls. A fake is a working but simplified implementation, such as an in-memory repository, that behaves realistically for many inputs. Fakes support more varied tests, but must be kept behaviourally close to the real thing.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you handle test data across several services?
interviewQuestions.a: Create data through each service's public API in the correct order, use unique identifiers per test, and avoid relying on shared mutable records. For reference data, seed known fixtures at environment start-up. Clean-up should be automated or environments should be ephemeral.

roles.codingRequirements: Moderate: one language for automation, plus Docker and configuration skills.
commonMistakes: Depending on shared, unstable integration environments for everything
Not testing failure modes of dependencies
Verifying responses but not side effects
readinessCriteria: You have built a containerised integration environment with at least one stubbed dependency
You can test retries and timeouts deterministically
You can explain when to use contract tests instead of integration tests

roles.title: Contract Testing Specialist
roles.overview: A Contract Testing Specialist helps teams verify that services agree on their interfaces without needing all services deployed together. They introduce and run consumer-driven contract testing, usually with Pact, and set up the workflow that lets teams deploy independently with confidence. The role mixes technical implementation with coaching multiple teams.
responsibilities: Introduce consumer-driven contract testing between services
Write consumer tests that generate contracts and provider verification tests
Set up a broker to share contracts and verification results
Integrate contract checks into CI and deployment gates
Coach teams on writing focused, maintainable contracts
Analyse contract failures and help teams resolve breaking changes

essential: Programming in at least one language used by the services
Pact or a similar contract testing tool
Understanding of service versioning and deployment
roleSpecific: Deployment safety checks with a contract broker

beginner.title: Why contracts
goals: Explain what a contract is and how it differs from a schema
Describe the consumer-driven contract workflow
Validate responses against JSON Schema

intermediate.title: Implement Pact
goals: Write a consumer test that generates a pact
Verify the pact against a provider using provider states
Publish pacts and results to a broker

advanced.title: Contracts in delivery
goals: Gate deployments on contract compatibility
Roll out contract testing across several teams
Handle breaking changes safely

tools: Pact Broker or a hosted broker
exercises: Write a Pact consumer test for a client that calls GET /orders/{id}
Verify that pact against a provider and use a provider state to set up data
Introduce a breaking change in the provider and observe the verification failure

sampleProject.title: Consumer-driven contracts between two services
sampleProject.description: Build or take two small services where one consumes the other's API. Add Pact consumer tests, provider verification with provider states, a broker running in Docker, and CI pipelines that publish and verify contracts and check compatibility before deployment. Document the workflow.

interviewQuestions.q: What problem does contract testing solve?
interviewQuestions.a: It verifies that a consumer and provider agree on their interface without running both in a shared integrated environment. Each side tests independently against the contract, so incompatibilities are caught early and teams can deploy independently. It replaces many slow, brittle end-to-end tests for interface checking.

interviewQuestions.q: What is consumer-driven contract testing?
interviewQuestions.a: The consumer writes tests against a mock provider that record the interactions it needs, generating a contract. The provider then verifies it can satisfy those interactions by replaying them against the real provider. Contracts therefore only include what consumers actually use, so providers know which changes are safe.

interviewQuestions.q: What are provider states?
interviewQuestions.a: They are named preconditions in a contract, such as 'an order with ID 10 exists', that the provider sets up before verifying an interaction. They let the provider control test data without the consumer knowing implementation details.

interviewQuestions.q: How is contract testing different from schema validation?
interviewQuestions.a: Schema validation checks that responses match a declared structure, usually the provider's view of the API. Contract testing checks specific interactions that real consumers depend on, including request shapes and example values, and verifies them against the provider. Both are useful; contracts capture actual usage.

interviewQuestions.q: What should not go in a contract?
interviewQuestions.a: Business logic and exhaustive validation scenarios belong in the provider's own functional tests. Contracts should capture the shape and essential values consumers rely on, using matchers rather than exact values where possible. Over-specified contracts break on harmless changes.

roles.codingRequirements: Moderate: able to write unit-test-level code in the services' languages (commonly Java, JavaScript or Python).
commonMistakes: Using contracts to test provider business logic
Hard-coding exact values instead of matchers
Not explaining how contracts enable independent deployment
readinessCriteria: You have implemented a consumer and provider Pact flow end to end
You can explain provider states and matchers with examples
You have a CI pipeline that fails on an incompatible provider change

roles.title: Microservices Test Engineer
roles.overview: A Microservices Test Engineer designs and implements testing for systems composed of many independently deployed services. The challenges are distributed: network failures, eventual consistency, versioning, asynchronous messaging and observability. The role spans component tests, contract tests, a small set of end-to-end tests and resilience testing.
responsibilities: Define a test approach for each service and for interactions between services
Automate component tests with dependencies stubbed or containerised
Implement contract tests between services
Test resilience patterns such as timeouts, retries and circuit breakers
Test eventually consistent and asynchronous flows
Use logs, metrics and traces to diagnose distributed failures

optional: Message brokers such as Kafka or RabbitMQ

beginner.title: Service-level testing
goals: Explain how testing microservices differs from testing a monolith
Automate API tests for a single service
Run services locally with Docker Compose

intermediate.title: Between services
goals: Write component tests with dependencies stubbed
Add contract tests between two services
Test retries and timeouts

advanced.title: Distributed resilience
goals: Inject faults and verify graceful degradation
Test eventually consistent flows without fixed sleeps
Use traces to diagnose cross-service failures

exercises: Write a component test for one service with all downstream services stubbed
Stop a downstream service and verify the circuit breaker opens and the caller degrades gracefully
Test an eventually consistent update by polling for the expected state with a timeout

sampleProject.title: Test strategy and suite for a microservice demo
sampleProject.description: Run an open-source microservice demo application locally. Implement component tests for two services, contract tests between them, a few end-to-end journeys, and a fault-injection test showing graceful degradation. Document the test pyramid you chose and how failures are diagnosed with traces.

interviewQuestions.q: How is testing microservices different from testing a monolith?
interviewQuestions.a: Failures happen over the network, so timeouts, partial failures and retries become normal scenarios. Services deploy independently, so interface compatibility needs continuous checking through contract tests. End-to-end tests become more expensive, and observability is essential to locate failures.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test eventual consistency?
interviewQuestions.a: After triggering the change, I poll the downstream state until it matches the expectation or a reasonable timeout expires, rather than sleeping for a fixed time. I also test what users see in the meantime and what happens when the propagation fails, such as messages being retried or sent to a dead-letter queue.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a circuit breaker and how would you test it?
interviewQuestions.a: It stops calls to a failing dependency after a threshold of failures, returning a fallback quickly, and periodically allows trial calls to see if the dependency has recovered. I would make a stubbed dependency fail, verify the breaker opens after the threshold and fallbacks are returned, then restore the dependency and verify it closes.

interviewQuestions.q: How many end-to-end tests should a microservice system have?
interviewQuestions.a: As few as needed to cover critical user journeys across the system, because they are slow and fragile. Most confidence should come from service-level and contract tests. The exact number depends on risk, but end-to-end tests should not be the main safety net.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you diagnose a failure that spans five services?
interviewQuestions.a: Use distributed tracing or correlation IDs to see the request path, latency and errors at each hop. Then examine logs and metrics for the service where the error originated. Reproduce at the narrowest scope, such as a component test, before reporting.

roles.codingRequirements: Moderate to strong: automation in a backend language, Docker, and comfort reading service code and configuration.
commonMistakes: Proposing a large end-to-end suite as the main strategy
Using fixed sleeps for asynchronous flows
Ignoring observability in failure diagnosis
readinessCriteria: You have tested a multi-service system with component and contract tests
You have run a fault-injection test and verified graceful degradation
You can explain your test pyramid choices for a distributed system

roles.title: Database Test Engineer
roles.overview: A Database Test Engineer verifies the correctness, integrity and behaviour of databases and the code that uses them: schemas, constraints, stored procedures, migrations, queries and transactions. Strong SQL is the core skill. The role is common where data accuracy is critical, such as finance, healthcare and enterprise systems.
responsibilities: Verify schemas, constraints, indexes and relationships match design
Test stored procedures, functions, triggers and views
Test schema migrations and rollback scripts
Validate data integrity after application operations
Test transactional behaviour and isolation
Identify slow queries and support performance analysis

essential: Advanced SQL: joins, aggregates, subqueries and window functions
optional: Scripting in Python for data checks
Database unit testing frameworks such as pgTAP or tSQLt

beginner.title: SQL for testing
goals: Write SELECT queries with filters, joins and grouping
Explain primary keys, foreign keys and constraints
Verify application data with SQL

intermediate.title: Test the database itself
goals: Test constraints by attempting invalid inserts
Test a stored procedure with boundary inputs
Test a migration on a copy of realistic data

advanced.title: Integrity and performance
goals: Test transaction isolation behaviour
Identify missing indexes using query plans
Automate database checks in CI

exercises: Write queries that find orphaned records, duplicates and invalid statuses in a sample database
Test a migration that splits a column into two, including rollback
Run two transactions concurrently at different isolation levels and record the anomalies observed

sampleProject.title: Database test suite for a sample schema
sampleProject.description: Use a publicly available sample database (such as a PostgreSQL sample schema) in Docker. Write automated tests for constraints, a stored function, data integrity queries and a migration with rollback, run them in CI, and document query plans for two slow queries with the indexes you tested.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you find duplicate records in a table?
interviewQuestions.a: Group by the columns that define uniqueness and filter groups with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1. To see the full rows, join back to the table or use a window function like ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by those columns. Then I would check whether a unique constraint should prevent this.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test a database migration?
interviewQuestions.a: Run it on a copy of realistic data, verify the schema changes, check data was transformed correctly with row counts and spot checks, and confirm the application works against the new schema. Test the rollback script too, and measure execution time on representative data volumes because long locks can cause outages.

interviewQuestions.q: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN?
interviewQuestions.a: INNER JOIN returns only rows with matches in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table, with NULLs where there is no match on the right. LEFT JOIN with a WHERE right.id IS NULL is a common test query to find orphaned or missing records.

interviewQuestions.q: Explain a dirty read and which isolation level prevents it.
interviewQuestions.a: A dirty read is when a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed and might be rolled back. The Read Committed isolation level and stricter levels prevent it. Note that some databases, such as PostgreSQL, never allow dirty reads even at Read Uncommitted.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test referential integrity?
interviewQuestions.a: Attempt to insert a child row with a non-existent parent and delete a parent with existing children, and check the database rejects or cascades as designed. I also run queries to find any existing orphans, since constraints may have been added after data was loaded.

roles.codingRequirements: Strong SQL is mandatory. Light scripting (Python or shell) is useful for automation.
commonMistakes: Only verifying data through the UI
Forgetting to test migration rollback and duration
Confusing join types under pressure
readinessCriteria: You can write queries with joins, grouping and window functions without reference
You have tested a migration including rollback on realistic data
You can explain isolation levels and demonstrate one anomaly

roles.title: Data Validation Tester
roles.overview: A Data Validation Tester checks that data is accurate, complete and consistent as it moves between systems: through imports, APIs, integrations and migrations. The work is reconciliation-heavy, comparing sources and targets and validating business rules on data. It is an accessible role for SQL-strong testers and a stepping stone towards data QA.
responsibilities: Validate data imports and exports against source files and rules
Reconcile record counts, totals and key fields between systems
Check data formats, ranges and mandatory fields
Test data migrations for completeness and correctness
Investigate and report data discrepancies with evidence
Maintain reusable validation queries and scripts

optional: Data quality tools such as Great Expectations

beginner.title: Validate data
goals: Write SQL to count, sum and filter records
Validate field formats and mandatory values
Read CSV, JSON and XML files confidently

intermediate.title: Reconcile
goals: Reconcile counts and totals between two systems
Find missing and extra records with joins
Validate data written by an API

advanced.title: Migrations and pipelines
goals: Plan and execute migration validation
Automate reconciliation checks
Validate transformations in an ETL flow

exercises: Reconcile a CSV import against the database table, reporting missing, extra and mismatched rows
Write validation queries for dates, ranges, null mandatory fields and invalid codes
Validate a simulated migration by comparing aggregated totals by category

sampleProject.title: Reconciliation toolkit for a data import
sampleProject.description: Create a sample source CSV and load it into a database with a deliberately imperfect import script. Build SQL and Python reconciliation checks covering counts, totals, key matches, formats and business rules, then produce a discrepancy report with evidence and suggested fixes.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you reconcile source and target data?
interviewQuestions.a: Start with counts and aggregate totals by meaningful groups, which find large problems quickly. Then compare at key level to find missing, extra and mismatched records, using joins on business keys. Finally, sample detailed field comparisons, especially for transformed fields.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you find records in table A that are missing from table B?
interviewQuestions.a: Use a LEFT JOIN from A to B on the business key and filter where B's key IS NULL, or use NOT EXISTS. EXCEPT works for comparing full rows in databases that support it. I watch out for NULLs in keys and differences in data types or whitespace that break matching.

interviewQuestions.q: What data quality dimensions do you check?
interviewQuestions.a: Completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity against formats and rules, uniqueness and timeliness. For each, I define concrete checks, such as no null mandatory fields or no duplicate customer IDs. This turns 'data looks wrong' into measurable findings.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you validate a large migration when you cannot check every row?
interviewQuestions.a: Combine full-volume automated checks, such as counts, totals and key matching, with targeted sampling of high-risk records like edge cases and records with special characters or unusual histories. I also confirm key business processes work on migrated data.

roles.codingRequirements: Solid SQL required; Python with pandas is a strong advantage.
commonMistakes: Checking only row counts
Ignoring NULL handling and data type differences in comparisons
Reporting discrepancies without query evidence
readinessCriteria: You can write reconciliation queries finding missing, extra and mismatched records
You have validated a file import end to end with documented results
You can name data quality dimensions with a concrete check for each

roles.title: Messaging and Event-Driven Systems Tester
roles.overview: A Messaging and Event-Driven Systems Tester verifies systems that communicate through message brokers and event streams such as Kafka, RabbitMQ or cloud queues. Testing focuses on asynchronous behaviour: ordering, duplicates, retries, dead-letter handling, schema evolution and eventual consistency. It requires a different mindset from request-response API testing.
responsibilities: Test producers and consumers of messages and events
Verify message schemas and their evolution
Test delivery guarantees, duplicates and idempotent consumers
Test ordering, retries and dead-letter queue behaviour
Verify end-to-end asynchronous flows and eventual consistency
Build tooling to publish and inspect messages in test environments

essential: Programming in one language with a messaging client
Messaging concepts: topics, queues, partitions and consumer groups
Asynchronous test design without fixed sleeps
optional: Schema registries and Avro or Protobuf

beginner.title: Messaging fundamentals
goals: Explain queues versus topics and consumer groups
Publish and consume messages locally in Docker
Validate message payloads against a schema

intermediate.title: Asynchronous behaviour
goals: Test that consumers handle duplicate messages safely
Test retries and dead-letter routing for poison messages
Assert on eventual outcomes by polling with timeouts

advanced.title: Robust event systems
goals: Test schema evolution for backwards and forwards compatibility
Add message contract tests
Test behaviour under consumer failure and broker restarts

tools: Kafka UI tools or command-line clients
exercises: Publish the same event twice and verify the consumer's side effect happens once
Send a malformed message and verify it lands in the dead-letter queue after the configured retries
Change an event schema by adding a field and test that existing consumers still work

sampleProject.title: Event-driven order pipeline tests
sampleProject.description: Build or run a small order system where an order service publishes events to Kafka or RabbitMQ and a fulfilment service consumes them. Using Testcontainers, write automated tests for happy path, duplicates, poison messages and dead-lettering, ordering within a key, and schema evolution, asserting on eventual outcomes without fixed sleeps.

interviewQuestions.q: What does at-least-once delivery mean for testing?
interviewQuestions.a: A message may be delivered more than once, for example after a consumer crashes before acknowledging. Consumers must therefore be idempotent, and I test this by delivering duplicate messages and verifying the side effect happens only once. Ignoring duplicates is a common source of double charges or duplicate records.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test asynchronous processing without flaky sleeps?
interviewQuestions.a: I poll for the expected outcome, such as a database record or an output message, at short intervals until it appears or a timeout expires, using a library like Awaitility or a simple retry loop. The timeout reflects the agreed processing expectation. This is both faster and more reliable than fixed sleeps.

interviewQuestions.q: What is a dead-letter queue and how do you test it?
interviewQuestions.a: It is a destination for messages that cannot be processed after a configured number of attempts, so they do not block the main flow. I send a poison message, verify the retries occur as configured, the message lands in the dead-letter queue with useful metadata, and that subsequent valid messages still process.

interviewQuestions.q: How does Kafka ordering work, and what would you test?
interviewQuestions.a: Kafka guarantees ordering only within a partition, and messages with the same key go to the same partition by default. I would test that events for one entity, keyed consistently, are processed in order, and check behaviour if a consumer must handle out-of-order events across keys or during rebalancing.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you test schema evolution?
interviewQuestions.a: I verify the compatibility rules in use, for example that adding an optional field does not break old consumers and that new consumers can read old messages. With a schema registry I test that incompatible changes are rejected. I also run consumers of the previous version against messages from the new producer.

roles.codingRequirements: Moderate: programming in a language with messaging clients (Java, Python or JavaScript), Docker, and asynchronous test patterns.
commonMistakes: Assuming exactly-once delivery without verifying how it is achieved
Using fixed sleeps in asynchronous tests
Assuming global ordering across Kafka partitions
